items.title: Booking a Hostel
lines: Hello, Sunrise Hostel. How can I help?
Hi, I'd like to book a bed for three nights, from the twelfth of July.
Let me check. We have a bed in a six-person room, or a private room for two.
How much is the private room?
It's thirty-five dollars a night, including breakfast. The shared room is twelve.
I'll take the shared room. I'm travelling on a budget. Is there somewhere to leave my bags?
Yes, there are lockers, but you need to bring your own lock, or you can buy one here for three dollars.
Great. And how do I get to you from the bus station?
Take bus number eight and get off at the market. We're opposite the post office.

qs.q: How many nights does the caller want?
Why does the caller choose the shared room?
Where is the hostel?

items.title: A Radio Announcement
items.text: And now some local news. Because of the heavy rain this week, the outdoor music festival planned for Saturday in Central Park has been moved indoors. It will now take place at the City Sports Hall on Le Loi Street. The start time has also changed: doors will open at five, not four, and the first band will play at six. Tickets already bought are still valid, but there are fewer places inside, so the organisers are asking people without tickets not to come. Free buses will run from the park to the sports hall every fifteen minutes from half past four. Food stalls will be available in the car park, so please don't bring your own food or drink into the hall.

qs.q: Why has the festival moved?
w: Because the park is closed for building

qs.q: What time will the doors open?
What are people asked not to do?
qs.a: Bring their own food and drink into the hall

items.title: Weekend Plans
lines: Are you doing anything this weekend, Nam?
I was going to go hiking with my brother, but he's hurt his knee playing football.
Not really, but the doctor told him to rest for two weeks. So now I've got no plans.
Why don't you come to the cooking class with me on Saturday? It's Thai food this week.
Sounds fun, but I'm terrible at cooking. Last time I tried to make rice, I burned the pan.
That's exactly why you should come! The teacher is really patient, and we eat everything at the end.
Well, if there's free food, how can I say no? What time does it start?
Ten o'clock. I'll pick you up at half past nine.

qs.q: Why can't Nam go hiking?
qs.a: His brother has a knee injury

qs.q: What does Nam say about his cooking?
qs.a: He is very bad at it

qs.q: What finally makes Nam agree?
qs.a: They can eat the food at the end
w: His friend will cook for him

items.title: A Museum Guide
items.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the City History Museum. My name is Thu and I'll be your guide today. The tour takes about an hour. We'll start here on the ground floor, where you can see objects from the first villages in this area, more than two thousand years ago. Then we'll go up to the first floor to look at the old port, which made the city rich in the seventeenth century. Please don't use flash when you take photos, because the light can damage the old paintings. If you need the toilets, they're behind the gift shop. At the end of the tour, there's a short film in our cinema room, and after that you're welcome to visit the café on the top floor, which has a great view of the river.

qs.q: How long is the tour?
Why can't visitors use flash?
w: It is not allowed in the cinema

qs.q: What can visitors see from the café?

items.title: At the Doctor's
lines: So, what seems to be the problem?
I've had a headache for about four days, and I feel tired all the time.
Not really. I've been working late on a big project, and I usually go to bed after midnight.
And how much water do you drink during the day?
Hmm, not much. Mostly coffee, maybe four or five cups.

That could be part of the problem. Too much coffee and not enough water can cause headaches. I don't think you need medicine. Try to drink two litres of water a day, cut down to two coffees, and go to bed before eleven.
And if the headache doesn't go away?
Then come back next week and we'll do some tests.

qs.q: How long has the patient had a headache?
What does the doctor think may be causing the problem?
qs.a: Too much coffee and too little water

qs.q: What does the doctor give the patient?

items.title: A Student's Talk about Recycling
items.tvi: Bài nói của học sinh về tái chế
items.text: For my project, I wanted to find out how much rubbish my family produces in one week. Every day, I weighed our bin before we emptied it. The total was eleven kilos, which surprised everyone. More than half was food waste, mostly vegetable peel and rice. The rest was plastic packaging, paper and a few glass bottles. So, in the second week, we made some changes. We started putting food waste in a compost box in the garden, and my mum began taking her own bags and boxes to the market. We also stopped buying bottled water and bought a filter instead. At the end of the second week, our rubbish was down to four kilos. My dad says the compost has already made his tomatoes grow better, so now he's the biggest fan of the project.

qs.q: What was most of the family's rubbish?
What did the mother start doing?
qs.a: Taking her own bags and boxes to the market

qs.q: Why does the father like the project now?
w: The family saves money on water
He weighs the bin every day

items.title: Changing a Flight
lines: Good afternoon, Sky Air customer service.
Hello, I'm booked on the flight to Da Nang on Friday morning, but I need to change it to Saturday.
Can I have your booking number, please?
Thank you. There's a Saturday flight at eight fifteen and another at three in the afternoon.
The afternoon one, please. I have a meeting on Saturday morning.
No problem. There's a change fee of two hundred thousand dong, and the afternoon flight is also fifty thousand more expensive.
So two hundred and fifty thousand in total?
That's right. I can take payment by card now, and I'll send the new ticket by email.

qs.q: When does the caller want to fly now?
Why doesn't the caller choose the morning flight?
How much extra will the caller pay in total?

items.title: A New Library
items.text: The new city library will open to the public on Monday, the fifth of May. The building has four floors. On the ground floor there's a children's area with games and a storytelling corner, which is open every afternoon from three until six. The first and second floors have books, newspapers and around a hundred computers that anyone can use for free for up to two hours a day. The top floor is a quiet study area for students, and you'll need to book a seat online. Membership is free for everyone who lives in the city. Just bring an identity card and a recent bill with your address on it. On opening day, the first five hundred visitors will receive a free cloth bag.

qs.q: When is the storytelling corner open?
What must you do to use the top floor?
What do you need to become a member?
qs.a: An identity card and a bill showing your address
w: A photo and a membership fee

items.title: Choosing a Present
lines: It's Grandma's seventieth birthday next week. Have you got any ideas for a present?
What about a new phone? Hers is really old.
I thought about that, but she says she hates learning new technology. She only uses it to call us.
She has a whole garden full of flowers. I was thinking of something more personal.
How about a photo book? We could collect old family photos and put them together with short messages from everyone.
That's a lovely idea. She's always telling stories about when Dad was little.
I'll ask Uncle Hai for the old pictures. He's got boxes of them.
Perfect. Let's order it online by Wednesday so it arrives in time.

qs.q: Why don't they buy Grandma a phone?
w: She already has a new one

qs.q: What present do they choose?
Who will provide the old pictures?

items.title: A Cycling Tour
items.text: Hi everyone, I'm Long, and I'll be leading today's cycling tour through the countryside. We'll ride about twenty-five kilometres in total, but don't worry, the road is mostly flat and we'll stop every forty-five minutes. Our first stop is a village where people make rice paper by hand. You can try making some yourself. After that we'll cycle along the river to a family farm, where we'll have lunch. The lunch is included in your ticket, but drinks are not. Please wear your helmet at all times, even if it's hot. If you have any problems with your bike, ring your bell twice and my colleague Mai, who rides at the back, will stop to help you. We should be back here at about four o'clock.

qs.q: What can visitors do at the first stop?
What is NOT included in the ticket?
What should people do if their bike has a problem?
